skill.name: bosai-typhoon
skill.description: 気象庁の台風情報JSONで現在発生中の台風の有無と情報を確認する。台風、台風何号、台風接近、進路の質問に対応。APIキー・ログイン不要。地震・津波・気象警報はbosai-alert、天気予報はjma-weather、雨雲はamagumoを使う。
skill.summary: Check the JMA typhoon feed, distinguish unavailable data from reported absence, and include the check time and official safety sources.
skill.author: tahodev

security_audit.summary: All six static findings are false positives in the reviewed SKILL.md. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential access, data exfiltration, or destructive filesystem operations.

static_findings.pattern: [HEURISTIC] High file entropy (6.91 bits) - possible binary/encrypted content

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 18 opens a Markdown bash fence, not Ruby or shell command substitution. The enclosed command retrieves a fixed public JMA URL without interpolation.
Line 20 closes the Markdown code fence. The following text describes HTTP status handling and contains no backtick execution.
The fixed HTTPS URL retrieves public JMA typhoon data using curl with a 30-second timeout. No credentials, local files, or user data are transmitted by this command.
The URL points users to the official JMA disaster information map for human verification. It is a contextual reference, not an upload destination.
Line 36 contains a fixed relative Markdown link to shared documentation. It does not use attacker-controlled paths or request file writes or unauthorized access.

The complete file is readable Japanese and English Markdown with YAML frontmatter and one plain curl example. No evidence found of binary payloads, encryption, encoded commands, or concealed instructions.

content.value_statement: Missing typhoon information and failed retrievals can look similar. This skill checks the public JMA feed, explains response status, and includes verification times and official safety references.
actual_capabilities: Retrieve the public JMA typhoon list without an API key or login.
Read an HTTP 200 array response and report the available typhoon information.
Treat HTTP 404 as no active typhoon information, following the documented September 11, 2026 observation.
Distinguish retrieval failures from reported absence and retry failures once or twice.
Include the check time and refer users to JMA and municipal announcements for safety decisions.
limitations: Active-typhoon fields, detailed payload structure, and tropical depression coverage were not verified when the skill was recorded.
The HTTP 404 absence interpretation rests on a September 11, 2026 observation, not a documented availability guarantee.
The skill requires network access and curl execution capability; earthquake alerts, forecasts, and rain radar are outside its scope.
The referenced shared response checklist is not included in the reviewed single-file package.

use_cases.title: Check Before Household Preparations
use_cases.description: Check whether the JMA feed reports typhoon information, then consult official announcements before making household safety decisions.

use_cases.title: Verify Information Before Travel
use_cases.description: Request a timestamped typhoon information check and an official JMA reference before reviewing travel plans.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Status Brief
use_cases.description: Summarize the feed status while clearly separating unavailable data from reported absence.

prompt_templates.title: Check Current Information
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether JMA currently reports active typhoon information. Include the check time and a link to official announcements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: a basic feed status check

prompt_templates.title: Report Available Typhoon Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve the JMA typhoon list and summarize only fields present in the response. Do not invent storm numbers, tracks, or local impacts.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Failed Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the JMA typhoon feed. Retry retrieval failures once or twice, then report the failure clearly without claiming that no typhoon exists.

prompt_templates.title: Draft an Operations Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a timestamped JMA typhoon status brief. Separate observed data from unknown details and cite official announcements for safety decisions.

output_examples.input: Illustrative scenario: the JMA list returns HTTP 404 at 09:00 JST.
output_examples.output: At 09:00 JST, the JMA list returned HTTP 404. The skill interprets this as no active typhoon information, based on its recorded observation. Check current JMA and municipal announcements before making safety decisions.

output_examples.input: Illustrative scenario: the JMA request times out and retries also fail at 09:05 JST.
output_examples.output: At 09:05 JST, the JMA typhoon feed could not be retrieved after retries. This does not establish that no typhoon exists. Review the official JMA disaster information map and municipal announcements.

output_examples.input: Illustrative scenario: HTTP 200 returns typhoon entries, but their detail fields are unfamiliar.
output_examples.output: The JMA list returned typhoon information. Detailed fields were not verified when this skill was recorded. Report only observed values and consult the official JMA map for further confirmation.

best_practices: Include the check time in every status report.
Keep HTTP status, retrieval failures, and reported absence distinct.
Consult JMA and municipal announcements before making evacuation or other safety decisions.
anti_patterns: Reporting no typhoon after a timeout or server failure.
Inventing typhoon numbers, tracks, field meanings, or local impacts.
Using this feed check as the sole basis for a safety decision.

faq.question: Do I need an API key or account?
faq.answer: No. The skill uses a public JMA endpoint without an API key or login.

faq.question: What does HTTP 404 mean here?
faq.answer: The skill interprets HTTP 404 as no active typhoon information, based on a September 11, 2026 observation. Confirm safety information through official announcements.

faq.question: What happens when the request fails?
faq.answer: The skill retries retrieval failures once or twice, then reports failure. It must not describe unavailable data as no typhoon.

faq.question: Can it provide verified typhoon tracks and detailed fields?
faq.answer: Active-typhoon payload fields were not verified when the skill was recorded. It should report observed data without guessing undocumented details.

faq.question: Does it cover earthquakes, forecasts, or rain radar?
faq.answer: No. The skill directs those requests to other skills, which are not included in this reviewed package.

faq.question: Can I use its result to decide whether to evacuate?
faq.answer: Do not rely on this skill alone. Follow current JMA and municipal announcements for evacuation and other safety decisions.
